newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** The Bombay High Court on Monday dismissed a petition seeking to stop Enron Corp of the U.S. from pursuing its Dabhhol power project on India's western coast.

Enron Corporation said it was pleased with the court decision to dismiss the only remaining lawsuit filed against its Dabhol Power Company. "This is the last critical step in getting the Dabhol Power Project back on track for completion by December 1998," Kenneth Lay, Enron's chairman and CEO said in a statement.
** A group of minority Indian shareholders of Sandoz (India) Ltd has launched a proxy war to oppose the terms of the merger of the company with Hindustan Ciba-Geigy Ltd, the Economic Times says.
This is the first time an Indian affiliate of a multinational is facing a proxy war from minority domestic shareholders.
** India's merchandise exports grew 8.4 percent to $2.68 billion in October compared to $2.47 billion in the same month in 1995, the government said.
** The cumulative growth in industrial production of 172 industries dropped to 8.6 percent during April-August from 8.9 percent during April-July this year, the Observer says.
** The Indian rupee opened Tuesday at 35.70/71 per dollar, unchanged from Monday's close, dealers said. The rupee expected to trade between 35.69 and 35.72 per dollar, they said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) .BSESN 30-share index fell 39.07 points, or 1.35 percent to end at 2,851.43 on Monday in a day that lacked action.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) .NSEI dropped 10.07 points to 820.25.
** The Delhi share index .DE lost 9.35 points to 639.64.
** The Madras exchange index .MDSI was down 15.99 points to 2,932.81.
